title.ko: 속담·반어·절제: a blessing in disguise · not bad at all · how wonderful, another delay

explain.ko: 속담은 오랜 경험을 담은 짧은 문장이고(A stitch in time saves nine), 관용구는 전체 뜻이 단어 하나하나와 다른 표현입니다(a blessing in disguise). 반어(irony)는 말한 것과 반대를 뜻하며, 절제된 표현(understatement)은 실제보다 약하게 말해 효과를 냅니다(not bad = very good). 비꼬는 어조(sarcasm)는 상대를 조롱하기 위해 쓰이므로 주의가 필요합니다. 해석할 때는 문맥과 어조를 반드시 확인해야 합니다.
explain.en: A proverb is a short saying from long experience (A stitch in time saves nine); an idiom has a whole meaning different from its words (a blessing in disguise). Irony means the opposite of what is said, and understatement says less than is meant for effect (not bad = very good). Sarcasm mocks someone, so use it with care. Always check context and tone when interpreting.

lines.t: Proverbs and irony are common in English. A proverb is a short saying from long experience, and irony means saying the opposite of what you mean. Understatement is deliberately saying less. For example, 'not bad' usually means very good.

trans.ko: 속담과 반어는 영어에서 자주 쓰입니다. 속담은 오랜 경험에서 나온 짧은 말이고, 반어는 실제 뜻과 반대로 말하는 표현입니다. 절제된 표현은 일부러 약하게 말하는 방식입니다. 예를 들어 '나쁘지 않네'는 보통 아주 좋다는 뜻입니다.

task.model: On the day I was late for an interview, it even poured with rain, but I arrived by the skin of my teeth. The interviewer smiled and said, 'Lovely weather today.' To say I was a little nervous is an understatement. In the end the experience was a blessing in disguise.

model_trans.ko: 면접에 지각한 날 비까지 쏟아졌지만, 나는 아슬아슬하게 도착했습니다. 면접관은 웃으며 '오늘 날씨가 참 좋네요'라고 말했습니다. 사실 조금 긴장했다고 말하는 것은 절제된 표현입니다. 결과적으로 그 경험은 전화위복이 되었습니다.
model_trans.en: On the day I was late for an interview, it even poured with rain, but I arrived by the skin of my teeth. The interviewer smiled and said, 'Lovely weather today.' To say I was a little nervous is an understatement. In the end the experience was a blessing in disguise.
